text:
Sam: Quick question — we need a clear precedence rule for route matching: when a route has both a header matcher and query-param matcher that could match the same request, which should win? e.g. /v1/payments?mode=fast vs header X-Mode:fast. Thoughts?
Tara: My instinct is: more-specific lexical match wins. But header vs query is not lexical. We should define a priority ordering: 1) exact host, 2) exact path, 3) header match, 4) query param, 5) wildcard/fallback. That would make header > query.
Miguel: We use query params a lot for feature flags (client-side) — putting header above query could break some customers. Also cache keys currently only include path+host, not query or header by default — changing precedence affects caching.
Olivia: UX note: console rules page should surface which field is authoritative and show evaluated example for a sample request. People get confused when multiple rules 'apply'.
Sam: Good point re cache keys. Do we want matching precedence to imply cache/key precedence? I.e., if header match wins, we should include that header in the cache key unless explicitly opted out.
Tara: Proposed minimal grammar (for runtime):
```
route := host_pattern path_pattern matchers action
matchers := (header | query | method | service)*
priority order := exact_host > exact_path > header > query > service_pattern > wildcard
```
Where header matches support exact and regex, and query only supports exact for now.
Miguel: Regex headers can be expensive at scale. Also service_pattern: if you have service:payments-v2 and path:/v1/payments — which do we evaluate first? I think service_pattern should be lower than path because path is user-facing.
Olivia: Also consider multi-tenant dedicated deployments: customers may want tenant-specific header overrides that should trump global query-based routing. Need an override layer: tenant > customer config > global.
Sam: So we're converging on: 1) scope precedence (tenant > customer > global), then 2) matching precedence within scope (host > path > header > query > service > wildcard). Anyone opposed?
Miguel: I want to flag quotas + telemetry: route attribution for quotas should follow the same precedence rules. If header won and that routes to a different bucket, quota usage should be charged to that route. Otherwise we'll have leakage.
Tara: Agree. Add to RFC: matching decision -> cache key generation -> quota attribution. Also add a toggle flag `include_in_cache_key` for headers/query on the route config. Default: header true, query false.
Olivia: For console UX, when editing a route we should show a computed preview: given sample request fields (host/path/headers/query), show the matched route and explain which matcher caused it. Small toggle: show alternate matches that lost and why.
Sam: Can someone draft a short RFC with examples and edge cases (regex headers, conflicting service patterns, cache key rules)? Miguel can you take quota+telemetry section? Tara you do runtime grammar and precedence. Olivia you do console/preview UX. I'll shepherd and merge.
Miguel: On it. Also: pinging @eng-sre — if header-in-cache-key default changes we need to run a rollout plan.
deploy-bot: config-lint: route-config.yaml: line 482: warning: header-regex under high-traffic route without precompiled regex flag. See: https://go.redwood/regex-precompile
Tara: Thanks deploy-bot — I'll add `precompile_regex: true` in examples.
Olivia: One more thought — telemetry: mark which matcher type matched (enum: HOST, PATH, HEADER, QUERY, SERVICE, WILDCARD) so downstream dashboards can filter by this.
Sam: Perfect. I'll create a draft RFC in the repo and link here by EOD. If anyone wants to add examples now paste them in this thread. :thumbsup:
